STRUCTURAL ASSESSMENT REPORT
Date of Inspection: January 20, 2026
Property: 987 Maple Dr, Houston TX

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
We assessed foundation and structural cracking reported after a plumbing leak was discovered on December 15, 2025. The property sits on expansive clay soil. Our assessment concludes the cracking is the result of long-term differential settlement and not related to the recent plumbing event.

FINDINGS:
We observed stair-step crack patterns in the exterior brick veneer on the east elevation. Interior drywall cracking was noted at door frames and window corners. The foundation exhibited lateral movement indicators. The property is 20 years old. We observed evidence of prior foundation repairs (piers on the west side).

No geotechnical analysis or soil testing was performed. No soil borings were taken. We did not review the previous foundation repair documentation. No elevation survey or level measurements were conducted. We did not install crack monitors to determine whether movement is active or historic.

The plumbing leak was located under the slab approximately 15 feet from the worst cracking. Water from the leak could have saturated the soil and contributed to soil movement. However, we attribute the damage to pre-existing settlement that has been ongoing for years based on the crack patterns and overall foundation condition.

CONCLUSION:
The structural damage is the result of long-term settlement related to the expansive soil conditions and is a pre-existing condition. The plumbing leak did not cause the foundation movement. This constitutes gradual deterioration, not sudden damage from a covered peril.
